text.p: Yemen's cabinet approved the 1997 national budget, with spending estimated at 313 billion rials ($3.13 billion) while revenues were forcast at 301 billion rials, a Yemeni official said on Thursday.

The budget, which carries a lower forecast deficit of 12 billion rials from the 25.53 billion projected for 1996, was approved in a cabinet session which was not attended by the second partner to President Ali Abdullah Saleh's General Peoples Congress, the Islah party.
"The cabinet approved in its extraordinary session today (Thursday) the general budget of the state for the coming year 1997," an unidentified official told Reuters.
Last year's state budget figures were estimated around 181.41 billion rials for national expenditure and 155.88 billion in revenues.

The official said ministers representing the Islamist Islah party walked out of Wednesday's session held to discuss the budget because it agreed on a merger of religious institutions and education ministry's budgets.
They did not attend Thursday's session either, he said.
Islah, headed by parliament speaker Sheikh Abdullah al-Ahmar, controls religous institutes where a special curriculum is followed.
Earlier this week, President Saleh called for the closing down of these institutes and merge them with those of the Education Ministry.
Now approved, the budget will be referred to the parliament for endorsement. Final approval should then be give by President Saleh.
